chunks: About a woman who freed one-third of her servant at the time of her death: are her heirs required to enter into a mukātabah contract with her if they wish, or if they refuse?

He said: "No. Rather, she owns one-third of herself, and the heir owns two-thirds of her. He may use her services in proportion to the share he has in her, and she has autonomy over herself in proportion to what has been emancipated of her."

key_terms.أَعْتَقَتْ: she emancipated or freed from bondage
key_terms.يَسْتَخْدِمُهَا: he uses her service according to ownership share
key_terms.يُكَاتِبُوهَا: to enter into a mukātabah contract with her for emancipation
key_terms.ٱلْوَارِثِ: the heir who inherits the remaining share

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a woman frees one-third of her servant at the time of her death?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on a servant partially emancipated by her mistress at death. It states that the emancipation takes effect according to the specified share, so the servant becomes free in that proportion while the remaining share stays with the heir, who retains rights only in proportion to that remainder.
